topic: How the Eras Tour Beat Elton John's Record (And Why It's Not the Same Race)

sentences.text: A billion-dollar tour just beat a record Elton John spent five years setting.
Pollstar says Taylor Swift's Eras Tour passed one billion dollars.
Elton John's farewell tour held the old record: nine hundred thirty-nine million dollars.
His total was built over five years, with pandemic delays.
Earlier record tours also played many more shows.
Same record, very different routes to get there.
sentences.editorial: framing of the comparison, not a research claim

sources.title: Taylor Swift breaks record with first tour to gross more than $1 billion (Music Week; exact day not retrieved, December 2023 per Pollstar reporting)
Taylor Swift's record breaking tour topped a billion dollars (Complete Music Update; exact day not retrieved)

claims.claim: Pollstar reported that Taylor Swift's Eras Tour had so far grossed more than $1 billion, the first tour to do so.
claims.excerpt: Taylor Swift’s Eras Tour has so far grossed more than $1 billion, according to Pollstar.
claims.context: Figure is a floor ('more than'), reported 'so far' in December 2023 and attributed to Pollstar. Headline: 'first tour to gross more than $1 billion'.

claims.claim: Elton John's Farewell Yellow Brick Road Tour set the previous touring record with $939 million.
claims.excerpt: Elton John’s Farewell Yellow Brick Road Tour set the previous touring record with $939 million
claims.context: The report's wording. Billboard's own Boxscore ranks only officially reported figures and is a different basis; this video uses the Music Week/Pollstar framing only.

claims.claim: Elton John's $939 million was amassed over five years, due to pandemic delays.
claims.excerpt: although that huge total was amassed over five years due to pandemic delays.
claims.context: Says nothing about how long the Eras Tour took, and the video says nothing either.

claims.claim: Previous record-breaking tours by U2, Ed Sheeran and Elton John all included many more performances.
claims.excerpt: making it bigger than previous record-breaking tours by U2, Ed Sheeran and Elton John which all included many more performances
claims.context: 'Many more performances' is the report's wording; no show counts were retrieved, so none are shown.
